extracted.intended_audience: marketers/PR professionals, authors, publishers, and brands looking to find Book Review YouTubers for outreach or collaboration
extracted.subtask_description: A curated directory of Book Review YouTube channels intended to help outreach/marketing campaigns and collaborations; entries are profiled with subscriber counts, social followings, bios, contact availability, and channel metadata. Use this list to discover channels by reach, niche, and contactability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following (YouTube subscribers)
rubrics_metrics.description: “When curating these Book Review youtubers, we’ve considered not just their following...” — each listing shows a 'YouTube Subscribers' count for the channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscriber numbers (e.g., 15.1K, 584K, 170K) are presented for each channel and are used as a primary measure of reach and scale when selecting channels for the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The curators state they considered 'engagement' when choosing channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specific engagement metrics (likes/comments/watch-time) are not shown per entry, engagement is invoked as a selection factor; implied supporting data includes 'Total Views' at the top and presence of activity notes in bios. Use engagement to assess how active/interactive a channel's audience is beyond raw subscriber counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall influence in the Book Review space
rubrics_metrics.description: The list was curated considering 'overall influence in the Book Review space.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influence includes editorial prestige, thought leadership, and community standing (examples: London Review of Books described as 'pre-eminent' and authoritative). This is a qualitative criterion combining reputation, visibility, and perceived authority within book discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel type / influencer tier
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry records 'Type of Channel' and a 'Type' tier (e.g., Influencer; Micro, Macro, Nano).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channels are categorized (nano/micro/macro) to indicate scale and typical campaign fit. Use tiers to match campaign budgets and goals (e.g., nano/micro for niche/affordable outreach; macro for broader reach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contactability / email availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings include 'Get Email Contact' and the page promotes exporting influencer contact lists and obtaining verified email contacts for outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of an email/contact and access to the Feedspot Influencers Contact Database is treated as important for facilitating collaborations and PR outreach; the page explicitly markets downloadable contact lists and an email (anuj@feedspot.com) to request influencer contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content focus / genre specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel bios explicitly state the kinds of books reviewed (romantasy, literary fiction, non-fiction, business books, comics, occult, children's/YA, spiritual, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre/niche focus is used to match channels to specific campaigns or readerships — the directory preserves each channel's stated focus so users can target reviewers relevant to their book/brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel age / longevity ('Since' date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each profile lists a 'Since' field showing when the channel started (e.g., Nov 2012, Apr 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longevity signals experience and potentially an established audience; use channel age as a proxy for consistency, archive depth, and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform reach (social followers & total views)
rubrics_metrics.description: Profiles include follower counts on other platforms (Twitter, Instagram, Facebook) and the page shows an aggregate 'Total Views' figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social follower counts and total views are presented alongside subscriber numbers to give a fuller picture of cross-platform influence; use these to evaluate multi-channel amplification potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience / demographic suitability and reviewer voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel descriptions frequently mention target audiences or reviewer perspective (e.g., 'preteens and teens', 'Youth Services librarian', 'personal opinion', 'student book reviews').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone, reviewer voice, and target demographic are surfaced in bios and should guide selection to ensure alignment with a brand's target reader demographic and desired review style (e.g., authoritative academic vs. casual enthusiastic fan).
